transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As we all know, we're reviewing the student oral-history project for the spring term before I give my final approval. The current draft has students in grades 7 and 8 participating, with one supervising adult per session, cloud-based audio storage, a 90-day retention period, and a public exhibit of selected recordings. I'd like to go through this systematically. Let's start with any concerns from your respective areas -- privacy, logistics, family communication, and classroom readiness. Who would like to begin?

transcript.text: I need to share some important findings from my classroom pilot. The pilot showed that this project is instructionally ready only for grade 8 — not grade 7. Additionally, each interview session requires exactly two supervising adults, not one, because students are working with recording equipment and community guests simultaneously. I recorded these findings in my end-of-pilot notes, but the current draft plan still contains the original scope of grades 7 and 8 and the one-adult staffing model. These need to be corrected before we move forward.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical privacy concern. The district privacy review, which I've completed, requires three things that differ from the current draft: first, recordings must remain on the district's encrypted internal server — not cloud-based storage; second, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the exhibit closes, not the 90-day retention period currently in the draft; and third, signed guardian consent must be obtained before any student records an interview. The draft still uses the preliminary cloud-storage language and doesn't reflect these requirements. These all need to be corrected before Dr. Chen signs off.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share findings from the archive and rights review I completed. The review permits each public exhibit audio excerpt to be no longer than exactly 3 minutes, and it requires contributor attribution beside every excerpt. I completed the rights check, but these limits have not yet been added to the exhibit template. The current draft doesn't reflect these requirements, and they need to be incorporated before Dr. Chen signs off.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share findings from the family outreach review I completed. Family outreach confirmed that consent materials must be available in exactly English, Spanish, and Arabic, and that paper consent forms must be offered in addition to the online form. I completed the outreach review, but the family-materials checklist has not yet been revised to reflect these requirements. This needs to be corrected before Dr. Chen signs off.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Revise the draft plan to reflect grade 8 only participation and two supervising adults per session, incorporating the end-of-pilot notes.
Update the plan to specify district encrypted internal server storage, 45-day deletion after exhibit closes, and signed guardian consent before recording.
Incorporate the 3-minute maximum excerpt length and contributor attribution requirement into the exhibit template.
Revise the family-materials checklist to include consent materials in English, Spanish, and Arabic, with paper consent forms offered alongside the online form.
Dr. Chen will sign off on the revised plan once all four corrections are documented and verified in the implementation records.
